tip: は = 'as for X' (what we are talking about). が = the one that does or exists, especially new information or the answer to who/what.
が points at the doer or the thing that exists. は sets the topic. 'Who came?' → 友達が来た. 'What about your friend?' → 友達は来た.
に = where something is / arrives (家にいる, 奈良に行く). で = where an action happens (家で食べる, 奈良で買う).
で marks the place of an action or the means. に marks arrival, existence, or a point in time.
に = arriving at. へ = heading toward. For destinations both work; に is more common in speech.
へ shows direction only. Use に for receivers (友達に話す), times (三時に), and existence (家にいる).
を = the thing acted on (お茶を飲む). が = the doer, or the thing that exists/is liked (お茶が好き, お茶がある).
With ある / いる / 好き / わかる / できる use が, not を.
を = object of the action. に = destination or receiver. 本を読む vs 友達に話す.
Go TO a place = に. Leave / pass through a place = を (家を出る, 道を歩く).
と = together with (both do it). に = toward one person (one-way): 友達と話す (chat together) vs 友達に話す (tell a friend).
に is one-directional (to someone). と is mutual (with someone).
から = start. まで = end. 九時から五時まで.
まで = until (continuing to that point). までに = by (deadline) — not in this course; use まで for 'until'.
も replaces は when adding 'also': 私は行く → 私も行く. Never say 私はも.
も replaces を: お茶を飲む → お茶も飲む. Never お茶をも.
と = with a person. で = by means of / at a place. 友達と行く, バスで行く.
Time words like 明日, 今日, 毎日 need no tag. Add は only to make them the topic (明日は休み).
Clock times and days of the week take に (三時に, 月曜日に). Relative times (明日, 今, 来週) take nothing.
